2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

11	/-!
12	# The finite Galois quotient engine (campaign milestone `G2`, scheme layer)
13	
14	Let `k'/k` be a finite Galois extension with group `Γ = Gal(k'/k)` and let `X'` be a
15	`k'`-scheme with a **semilinear** `Γ`-action.  This file supplies the scheme-level
16	vocabulary and statements for the quotient engine `G2` of the Picard representability
17	campaign (`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`, cluster `G`): the `k`-scheme
18	`X = X'/Γ` with `Γ`-equivariant `X ×_k k' ≅ X'` and
19	`Hom_k(T, X) ≅ Hom_{k'}(T_{k'}, X')^Γ`.
20	
21	## Semilinearity at scheme level (audit, campaign checklist item — conventions)
22	
23	A semilinear action is a group homomorphism `act : Γ →* Aut X'` together with
24	commuting squares over the Galois action on the base: `(act γ).hom ≫ f = f ≫ Spec γ`
25	(`SemilinearGalAction`).  Conventions are **validated constructively** by the affine
26	model `specSemilinearGalAction`: for `X' = Spec A` with a `MulSemiringAction Γ A`
27	that is `IsSemilinear K L A`, the assignment `γ ↦ Spec (γ⁻¹ • ·)` (`toSpecAut`) is a
28	group homomorphism into `Aut (Spec A)` — the inversion is forced jointly by the
29	contravariance of `Spec` and mathlib's `Aut` group law (`(x*y).hom = y.hom ≫ x.hom`)
30	— and satisfies the commuting squares.
31	
32	## Hironaka trap (campaign audit item 8, BLOCKING — verdict recorded here)
33	
34	The **orbit-in-affine hypothesis** (`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen`: every
35	`Γ`-orbit lies in an affine open) is **essential and non-technical**.  For a free
36	action of `ℤ/2` on Hironaka's smooth proper non-projective threefold swapping two
37	rational curves that meet no common affine open, the quotient does **not** exist as
38	a scheme (only as an algebraic space); this is the same counterexample genus as the
39	permanently-instance-free `HasSmoothProperQuotient` (`FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
40	Consequently the quotient existence is **never** stated for a bare `X'`: every
41	statement below carries the orbit hypothesis (or is a `Prop`-gate with **no
42	instances**).  For the campaign consumer `J'_r` the hypothesis is supplied by the
43	Γ-stable covering `V_Σ` with Grassmannian-immersion certificates (plan `J5`/`R6`).
44	
45	## Main definitions and results
46	
47	* `toSpecAut G A : G →* Aut (Spec A)` — a group acting on a ring by ring
48	  automorphisms acts on `Spec A` by scheme automorphisms.
49	* `SemilinearGalAction K L X f` — semilinear `Gal(L/K)`-action on a scheme over
50	  `Spec L`.
51	* `specSemilinearGalAction` — the affine model (conventions validator).
52	* `pullbackSemilinearGalAction` — the canonical action on a base change
53	  `T ×_{Spec K} Spec L` through the second factor (used to *state* equivariance of
54	  the descent isomorphism and the `T`-points property).
55	* `SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` — the orbit-in-affine hypothesis class.
56	* `IsGaloisQuotient ρ g` — the full quotient predicate: `Γ`-equivariant base-change
57	  isomorphism **and** the universal `T`-points property
58	  `Hom_k(T, X) ≅ Hom_{k'}(T_{k'}, X')^Γ` (unique descent of equivariant morphisms).
59	* `HasStableAffineCover` — Γ-stable affine refinement, the EGA II 4.5.4 pattern
60	  (`finite point set in an affine open of a separated/quasi-projective scheme
61	  refines to a Γ-stable affine open`). **This is no longer a gate: `G2(a)` was
62	  discharged** and `StableAffineCover.lean:279`
63	  (`hasStableAffineCover_of_orbitsInAffineOpen`) is a global `instance` deriving
64	  it from `[ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen]` alone. Measured (`review-ajc`, 2026-07-29):
65	  `infer_instance` succeeds for an *abstract* `ρ` carrying only the orbit
66	  hypothesis, and fails without it — so the orbit hypothesis is exactly what it
67	  costs. The three sentences in this file and in `FiniteGaloisQuotientAffine.lean`
68	  that called it instance-free predate that discharge.
69	* `HasGaloisQuotient` — `Prop`-gate. It **was** genuinely instance-free; it is not
70	  any more, and the residue is now precisely the **non-affine** case.
71	  `hasGaloisQuotient_of_isAffine` (`Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean`) is a
72	  global `instance` discharging it for `[IsAffine X]`, via transport of
73	  `isGaloisQuotient_spec` along the equivariant `X.isoSpec`. Measured both ways
74	  **from a file that imports that module** — the qualification is load-bearing and
75	  this file is two import hops *below* it, so neither claim can be reproduced here:
76	  `inferInstance` closes the goal at the formerly hand-built witness
77	  `hasGaloisQuotient_specF4`, and **fails** for an abstract `ρ` carrying the orbit
78	  hypothesis without affineness. So the remaining `G2(c)` work is the gluing of
79	  `Spec (A_U^Γ)` along a stable affine cover — the step the repaired
80	  representability route actually runs on, since its consumer `J'_r` is glued.
81	* `affineGaloisQuotientHomEquiv` — **the affine case of the Hom property, proved**:
82	  for `X' = Spec A` and affine `T = Spec B`,
83	  `Hom_{Spec K}(T, Spec A^Γ) ≃ Γ-invariant Hom_{Spec L}(T ×_K Spec L, Spec A)`,
84	  by Speiser descent (`SemilinearAlgebras.invariantAlgHomEquiv`) — never via
85	  Noether invariant finiteness.
86	
87	Campaign reference: `G2` of `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md` (consumed by
88	`G3`/`G4`; curve-agnostic, reusable for `Sym^d`/Albanese).  Sources: Milne, *Jacobian
89	Varieties* §4 and Kleiman, *The Picard scheme* (FGA explained) §4 use exactly this
90	finite Galois quotient to descend `Pic_{C_{k'}/k'}` to `k`; the affine heart is
91	Speiser's theorem.
92	-/

101	/-! ## Spec of a ring action -/
102	
103	section SpecAut
104	
105	variable (G : Type*) [Group G] (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [MulSemiringAction G A]
106	
107	lemma toRingHom_comp (γ τ : G) :
108	    (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A γ).comp (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A τ)
109	      = MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A (γ * τ) :=
110	  RingHom.ext fun x => (mul_smul γ τ x).symm
111	
112	lemma toRingHom_one : MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A (1 : G) = RingHom.id A :=
113	  RingHom.ext fun x => one_smul G x
114	
115	/-- A group acting on a commutative ring by ring automorphisms acts on `Spec A` by
116	scheme automorphisms: `γ` acts by `Spec (γ⁻¹ • ·)`.  The inversion is forced jointly
117	by the contravariance of `Spec` and the `Aut` group law, so that `toSpecAut` is a
118	group **homomorphism** (not an anti-homomorphism). -/
119	noncomputable def toSpecAut : G →* Aut (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) :=
120	  MonoidHom.mk'
121	    (fun γ =>
122	      { hom := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A γ⁻¹))
123	        inv := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A γ))
124	        hom_inv_id := by
125	          rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, toRingHom_comp,
126	            inv_mul_cancel, toRingHom_one, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]
127	        inv_hom_id := by
128	          rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, toRingHom_comp,
129	            mul_inv_cancel, toRingHom_one, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id] })
130	    (fun γ τ => by
131	      refine Iso.ext ?_
132	      change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A (γ * τ)⁻¹))
133	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A τ⁻¹)) ≫
134	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A γ⁻¹))
135	      rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, toRingHom_comp, ← mul_inv_rev])
136	
137	lemma toSpecAut_hom (γ : G) :
138	    (toSpecAut G A γ).hom
139	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A γ⁻¹)) := rfl
140	
141	lemma toSpecAut_mul_hom (γ τ : G) :
142	    (toSpecAut G A (γ * τ)).hom = (toSpecAut G A τ).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A γ).hom := by
143	  rw [map_mul]; rfl
144	
145	lemma toSpecAut_inv_hom (γ : G) :
146	    (toSpecAut G A γ⁻¹).hom = (toSpecAut G A γ).inv := by
147	  rw [map_inv]; rfl
148	
149	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
150	lemma toSpecAut_hom_inv_hom (γ : G) :
151	    (toSpecAut G A γ).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A γ⁻¹).hom = 𝟙 _ := by
152	  rw [toSpecAut_inv_hom, Iso.hom_inv_id]
153	
154	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
155	lemma toSpecAut_inv_hom_hom (γ : G) :
156	    (toSpecAut G A γ⁻¹).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A γ).hom = 𝟙 _ := by
157	  rw [toSpecAut_inv_hom, Iso.inv_hom_id]
158	
159	end SpecAut

161	/-! ## Semilinear Galois actions on schemes over `Spec L` -/
162	
163	variable (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
164	
165	/-- A **semilinear `Gal(L/K)`-action** on a scheme `X` over `Spec L` (campaign
166	`G2(a)`): a group homomorphism into scheme automorphisms of the total space, each
167	automorphism lying in a commuting square over the corresponding Galois automorphism
168	`Spec γ` of the base.  (`X` is *not* acted on over `Spec L` — only the composite
169	descends to `Spec K`; this is exactly Kleiman/Milne's "descent datum" for the finite
170	Galois cover `Spec L → Spec K`.) -/
171	structure SemilinearGalAction (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) where
172	  /-- The action by scheme automorphisms. -/
173	  act : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) →* Aut X
174	  /-- Each automorphism covers the Galois action `Spec γ` on the base. -/
175	  compat (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
176	    (act γ).hom ≫ f = f ≫ (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) L γ).hom
177	
178	namespace SemilinearGalAction
179	
180	variable {K L}
181	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
182	
183	/-- Equivariance of a morphism between two semilinearly-acted schemes over `Spec L`. -/
184	def IsEquivariant {X' : Scheme.{u}} {f' : X' ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
185	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (ρ' : SemilinearGalAction K L X' f')
186	    (h : X ⟶ X') : Prop :=
187	  ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (ρ.act γ).hom ≫ h = h ≫ (ρ'.act γ).hom
188	
189	/-- The `Γ`-orbit of a point of `X` under a semilinear action. -/
190	def orbit (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (x : X) : Set X :=
191	  Set.range fun γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (ρ.act γ).hom.base x
192	
193	/-- **Orbit-in-affine hypothesis** (campaign `G2`, audit item 8): every `Γ`-orbit is
194	contained in an affine open.  This hypothesis is **essential** (Hironaka trap — see
195	the module docstring): without it the quotient exists only as an algebraic space.
196	For finite Galois `L/K` every orbit is finite, so this is the standard EGA II 4.5.4
197	hypothesis; it holds e.g. for quasi-projective `X` (finite point sets of
198	quasi-projective schemes lie in affine opens) and is supplied to the campaign
199	consumer by the Γ-stable `V_Σ` covers of `J5`. -/
200	class OrbitsInAffineOpen (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
201	  exists_affineOpen (x : X) :
202	    ∃ U : X.affineOpens, ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (ρ.act γ).hom.base x ∈ U.1
203	
204	/-- A `Γ`-stable open of `X`. -/
205	def IsStableOpen (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (U : X.Opens) : Prop :=
206	  ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (ρ.act γ).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U = U
207	
208	end SemilinearGalAction
209	
210	/-- Campaign `G2(a)`, EGA II 4.5.4 pattern: a `Γ`-stable affine refinement — every
211	point admits a `Γ`-stable affine open neighbourhood.
212	
213	**This was a gate and is not one any more; the words "no instances" stood here after
214	its own discharge landed** (`review-ajc`, 2026-07-29 — and they survived one file away
215	from the module-header correction of the same error, which is why they are struck in
216	the class docstring too). `hasStableAffineCover_of_orbitsInAffineOpen`
217	(`Picard/StableAffineCover.lean:279`) is a global `instance` deriving this class from
218	`[FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] [ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen]` — the sanctioned
219	discharge, and the only one. Measured: `infer_instance` succeeds for an *abstract* `ρ`
220	carrying the orbit hypothesis and fails without it, so the orbit hypothesis is exactly
221	its price. `HasGaloisQuotient` below is the gate that remains (it fails to synthesize
222	even with the orbit hypothesis *and* this class in scope).
223	
224	The historical discharge recipe, kept because it records what the proof cost:
225	from `OrbitsInAffineOpen`, given an orbit inside affine `U`, prime avoidance produces
226	`s ∈ Γ(U, 𝒪)` with the orbit inside `D(s) ⊆ ⋂_γ γU`, and the product `∏_γ γ(s)` cuts
227	out a `Γ`-stable affine basic open — a genuine multi-session lemma (walls: transport
228	of sections along the action isomorphisms, and basic-open-affineness bookkeeping),
229	pinned here per the campaign plan ("may be pinned as a separate gated statement if it
230	walls"). -/
231	class HasStableAffineCover {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
232	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
233	  exists_stable_affineOpen (x : X) :
234	    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ ρ.IsStableOpen U
235	
236	/-! ## The affine model (conventions validator) -/
237	
238	section AffineModel
239	
240	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra K A] [Algebra L A] [IsScalarTower K L A]
241	variable [MulSemiringAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A]
242	
243	/-- The affine model of a semilinear Galois action: a `MulSemiringAction Γ A` that is
244	`IsSemilinear K L A` induces a semilinear action on `Spec A` over `Spec L`.  This
245	validates the sign/direction conventions of `SemilinearGalAction` constructively. -/
246	noncomputable def specSemilinearGalAction [IsSemilinear K L A] :
247	    SemilinearGalAction K L (Spec (CommRingCat.of A))
248	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L A))) where
249	  act := toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A
250	  compat γ := by
251	    rw [toSpecAut_hom, toSpecAut_hom, ← Spec.map_comp, ← Spec.map_comp,
252	      ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
253	    congr 2
254	    ext x
255	    exact SemilinearAction.smul_algebraMap K L A γ⁻¹ x
256	
257	end AffineModel

259	/-! ## The canonical action on a base change `T ×_{Spec K} Spec L` -/
260	
261	section PullbackAction
262	
263	/-- Each Galois automorphism of `Spec L` is a morphism over `Spec K`. -/
264	lemma toSpecAut_hom_comp_baseMap (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
265	    (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) L γ).hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))
266	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)) := by
267	  rw [toSpecAut_hom, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
268	  congr 2
269	  ext x
270	  exact AlgEquiv.commutes γ⁻¹ x
271	
272	variable {Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
273	
274	/-- The single automorphism of the base change `Y ×_{Spec K} Spec L` induced by
275	`γ` through the second factor. -/
276	noncomputable abbrev pullbackGalMap (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
277	    pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
278	      ⟶ pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) :=
279	  pullback.map g _ g _ (𝟙 Y) (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) L γ).hom (𝟙 _)
280	    (by simp) (by rw [Category.comp_id, toSpecAut_hom_comp_baseMap])
281	
282	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
283	lemma pullbackGalMap_fst (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
284	    pullbackGalMap K L g γ ≫ pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
285	      = pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) := by
286	  have h : pullbackGalMap K L g γ ≫ pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
287	      = pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ≫ 𝟙 Y :=
288	    pullback.lift_fst _ _ _
289	  rw [h, Category.comp_id]
290	
291	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
292	lemma pullbackGalMap_snd (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
293	    pullbackGalMap K L g γ ≫ pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
294	      = pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ≫
295	          (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) L γ).hom :=
296	  pullback.lift_snd _ _ _
297	
298	/-- The canonical semilinear Galois action on a base change
299	`Y ×_{Spec K} Spec L → Spec L` through the second factor.  This is the reference
300	action used to *state* equivariance of descent isomorphisms and the `T`-points
301	property. -/
302	noncomputable def pullbackSemilinearGalAction :
303	    SemilinearGalAction K L
304	      (pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))))
305	      (pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))) where
306	  act := MonoidHom.mk'
307	    (fun γ =>
308	      { hom := pullbackGalMap K L g γ
309	        inv := pullbackGalMap K L g γ⁻¹
310	        hom_inv_id := by
311	          apply pullback.hom_ext
312	          · rw [Category.assoc, pullbackGalMap_fst, pullbackGalMap_fst, Category.id_comp]
313	          · rw [Category.assoc, pullbackGalMap_snd, pullbackGalMap_snd_assoc,
314	              toSpecAut_hom_inv_hom, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]
315	        inv_hom_id := by
316	          apply pullback.hom_ext
317	          · rw [Category.assoc, pullbackGalMap_fst, pullbackGalMap_fst, Category.id_comp]
318	          · rw [Category.assoc, pullbackGalMap_snd, pullbackGalMap_snd_assoc,
319	              toSpecAut_inv_hom_hom, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp] })
320	    (fun γ τ => by
321	      refine Iso.ext ?_
322	      change pullbackGalMap K L g (γ * τ)
323	        = pullbackGalMap K L g τ ≫ pullbackGalMap K L g γ
324	      apply pullback.hom_ext
325	      · rw [Category.assoc, pullbackGalMap_fst, pullbackGalMap_fst, pullbackGalMap_fst]
326	      · rw [Category.assoc, pullbackGalMap_snd, pullbackGalMap_snd,
327	          pullbackGalMap_snd_assoc, toSpecAut_mul_hom])
328	  compat γ := pullback.lift_snd _ _ _
329	
330	@[simp] lemma pullbackSemilinearGalAction_act_hom (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
331	    ((pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L g).act γ).hom = pullbackGalMap K L g γ := rfl
332	
333	variable {T : Scheme.{u}} (t : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
334	
335	/-- The base change to `Spec L` of a morphism over `Spec K`. -/
336	noncomputable abbrev pullbackBaseChange (u : T ⟶ Y) (hu : u ≫ g = t) :
337	    pullback t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
338	      ⟶ pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) :=
339	  pullback.map t _ g _ u (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (by rw [Category.comp_id, hu]) (by simp)
340	
341	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
342	lemma pullbackBaseChange_fst (u : T ⟶ Y) (hu : u ≫ g = t) :
343	    pullbackBaseChange K L g t u hu ≫
344	        pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
345	      = pullback.fst t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ≫ u :=
346	  pullback.lift_fst _ _ _
347	
348	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
349	lemma pullbackBaseChange_snd (u : T ⟶ Y) (hu : u ≫ g = t) :
350	    pullbackBaseChange K L g t u hu ≫
351	        pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
352	      = pullback.snd t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) := by
353	  have h : pullbackBaseChange K L g t u hu ≫
354	        pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
355	      = pullback.snd t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ≫ 𝟙 _ :=
356	    pullback.lift_snd _ _ _
357	  rw [h, Category.comp_id]
358	
359	variable {K L}
360	
361	/-- Naturality of the base-change action: base changes of morphisms over `Spec K`
362	are equivariant for the canonical actions. -/
363	lemma pullbackGalMap_naturality (u : T ⟶ Y) (hu : u ≫ g = t) (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
364	    pullbackGalMap K L t γ ≫ pullbackBaseChange K L g t u hu
365	      = pullbackBaseChange K L g t u hu ≫ pullbackGalMap K L g γ := by
366	  apply pullback.hom_ext <;> simp
367	
368	/-- The base change of a morphism over `Spec K`, composed with an equivariant
369	morphism, is equivariant.  (The "easy direction" of the `T`-points property of a
370	Galois quotient: descended morphisms induce equivariant ones.) -/
371	theorem SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp
372	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
373	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
374	    {e : pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ⟶ X}
375	    (he : (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L g).IsEquivariant ρ e)
376	    (u : T ⟶ Y) (hu : u ≫ g = t) :
377	    (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L t).IsEquivariant ρ
378	      (pullbackBaseChange K L g t u hu ≫ e) := by
379	  intro γ
380	  rw [pullbackSemilinearGalAction_act_hom, ← Category.assoc,
381	    pullbackGalMap_naturality g t u hu γ, Category.assoc, Category.assoc]
382	  exact congrArg _ (he γ)
383	
384	end PullbackAction
385	
386	/-! ## The quotient predicate and the existence gate -/
387	
388	section Quotient
389	
390	variable {K L}
391	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
392	
393	/-- `(Y, g)` is a **finite Galois quotient** of the semilinearly-acted `(X, f, ρ)`
394	(campaign `G2`): there is an isomorphism `e : Y ×_{Spec K} Spec L ≅ X` which is
395	
396	1. over `Spec L`,
397	2. `Γ`-equivariant for the canonical base-change action, and
398	3. universal: every equivariant morphism `T ×_{Spec K} Spec L ⟶ X` over `Spec L`
399	   descends **uniquely** to `T ⟶ Y` over `Spec K` — this clause is exactly
400	   `Hom_K(T, Y) ≅ Hom_L(T_L, X)^Γ` (the inverse bijection direction is
401	   `SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackMap_comp`). -/
402	def IsGaloisQuotient (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
403	    (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) : Prop :=
404	  ∃ e : pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ≅ X,
405	    e.hom ≫ f = pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ∧
406	    (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L g).IsEquivariant ρ e.hom ∧
407	    ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (t : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
408	      (h : pullback t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ⟶ X),
409	      h ≫ f = pullback.snd t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) →
410	      (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L t).IsEquivariant ρ h →
411	      ∃! u : {u : T ⟶ Y // u ≫ g = t},
412	        pullbackBaseChange K L g t u.1 u.2 ≫ e.hom = h
413	
414	/-- GATE (campaign `G2`) — existence of the finite Galois quotient under the
415	orbit-in-affine hypothesis.
416	
417	**No longer instance-free, and the qualification matters: it is discharged on the
418	AFFINE locus** (`hasGaloisQuotient_of_isAffine`,
419	`Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean`, a global `instance`), so for `[IsAffine X]`
420	this class synthesizes outright and subsumes the former single-object witness
421	`hasGaloisQuotient_specF4`. Both measurements below are **from a file importing that
422	module**, which this one is two hops below, so do not expect to reproduce either
423	here: `inferInstance` closes the `𝔽₄` goal, and — the other direction — **fails** for
424	an abstract `ρ` carrying the orbit hypothesis but not affineness, so the remaining
425	content is exactly the non-affine case.
426	
427	Intended discharge of what is left (`G2(c)`): a `Γ`-stable affine cover
428	(`HasStableAffineCover`, from `OrbitsInAffineOpen` via the EGA II 4.5.4 pattern),
429	`Spec (A_U^Γ)` on each stable affine piece by Speiser descent
430	(`SemilinearAlgebras.descentAlgEquiv` — the affine Hom property is
431	`affineGaloisQuotientHomEquiv` below; the per-chart *quotient* is now the affine
432	instance above rather than something to re-derive), glued via `Scheme.GlueData`.
433	The orbit hypothesis is **essential** for that step (Hironaka trap — module
434	docstring), and the affine discharge does not weaken it: an affine `X` has no room
435	for the trap. -/
436	class HasGaloisQuotient [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
437	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) [ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen] : Prop where
438	  exists_quotient :
439	    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)), IsGaloisQuotient ρ g
440	
441	end Quotient
442	
443	/-! ## The left-factor Galois action on `L ⊗[K] B` -/
444	
445	section TensorAction
446	
447	variable (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra K B]
448	
449	/-- The left-factor Galois action `γ ↦ γ ⊗ id` on a base change `L ⊗[K] B`.
450	Scoped instance: mathlib carries no action of `L ≃ₐ[K] L` on tensor products, so no
451	diamond can arise; still scoped for hygiene since for `B = L` the *right*-factor
452	action is equally natural. -/
453	noncomputable scoped instance instMulSemiringActionTensor :
454	    MulSemiringAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) (L ⊗[K] B) where
455	  smul γ x := Algebra.TensorProduct.map (γ : L →ₐ[K] L) (AlgHom.id K B) x
456	  one_smul x := by
457	    change Algebra.TensorProduct.map _ _ x = x
458	    rw [show ((1 : L ≃ₐ[K] L) : L →ₐ[K] L) = AlgHom.id K L from rfl,
459	      Algebra.TensorProduct.map_id, AlgHom.coe_id, id_eq]
460	  mul_smul γ τ x := by
461	    change Algebra.TensorProduct.map _ _ x
462	      = Algebra.TensorProduct.map _ _ (Algebra.TensorProduct.map _ _ x)
463	    rw [← AlgHom.comp_apply, ← Algebra.TensorProduct.map_comp]
464	    rfl
465	  smul_zero γ := map_zero _
466	  smul_add γ := map_add _
467	  smul_one γ := map_one _
468	  smul_mul γ := map_mul _
469	
470	@[simp] lemma galTensor_smul_def (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (x : L ⊗[K] B) :
471	    γ • x = Algebra.TensorProduct.map (γ : L →ₐ[K] L) (AlgHom.id K B) x := rfl
472	
473	/-- The left-factor Galois action on `L ⊗[K] B` is semilinear. -/
474	instance : IsSemilinear K L (L ⊗[K] B) := by
475	  refine SemilinearAction.isSemilinear_of_smul_algebraMap K L _ fun γ a => ?_
476	  change Algebra.TensorProduct.map (γ : L →ₐ[K] L) (AlgHom.id K B)
477	      (algebraMap L (L ⊗[K] B) a) = algebraMap L (L ⊗[K] B) (γ a)
478	  have h : ∀ c : L, algebraMap L (L ⊗[K] B) c = c ⊗ₜ[K] (1 : B) := fun c => rfl
479	  rw [h, h, Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, map_one]
480	  rfl
481	
482	end TensorAction
483	
484	/-! ## Spec-side Hom bookkeeping -/
485	
486	section SpecHoms
487	
488	variable (R S₁ S₂ : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S₁] [CommRing S₂]
489	variable [Algebra R S₁] [Algebra R S₂]
490	
491	/-- Morphisms `Spec S₂ ⟶ Spec S₁` over `Spec R` are `R`-algebra maps `S₁ → S₂`
492	(affine relative Spec adjunction, triangle form). -/
493	noncomputable def specOverEquivAlgHom :
494	    {t : Spec (CommRingCat.of S₂) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of S₁) //
495	      t ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R S₁))
496	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R S₂))} ≃ (S₁ →ₐ[R] S₂) where
497	  toFun t :=
498	    { toRingHom := (Spec.preimage t.1).hom
499	      commutes' := fun r => by
500	        have h := t.2
501	        rw [← Spec.map_preimage t.1, ← Spec.map_comp] at h
502	        have h2 := congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (Spec.map_injective h)
503	        rw [CommRingCat.hom_comp, CommRingCat.hom_ofHom, CommRingCat.hom_ofHom] at h2
504	        exact DFunLike.congr_fun h2 r }
505	  invFun φ :=
506	    ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom), by
507	      rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
508	      congr 1
509	      exact CommRingCat.hom_ext (RingHom.ext fun r => φ.commutes r)⟩
510	  left_inv t := by
511	    apply Subtype.ext
512	    change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Spec.preimage t.1).hom) = t.1
513	    rw [CommRingCat.ofHom_hom, Spec.map_preimage]
514	  right_inv φ := by
515	    apply AlgHom.ext
516	    intro x
517	    change (Spec.preimage (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom))).hom x = φ x
518	    rw [Spec.preimage_map]
519	    rfl
520	
521	end SpecHoms
522	
523	/-! ## The affine case of the Hom property -/
524	
525	section AffineHomProperty
526	
527	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra K A] [Algebra L A] [IsScalarTower K L A]
528	variable [MulSemiringAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A] [IsSemilinear K L A]
529	variable [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
530	variable (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra K B]
531	
532	open SemilinearAction
533	
534	omit [Algebra K A] [IsScalarTower K L A] [IsSemilinear K L A]
535	  [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
536	/-- Equivariance of an `L`-algebra map matches equivariance of the corresponding
537	morphism of affine schemes (with the `toSpecAut` actions on both sides). -/
538	lemma isEquivariantAlgHom_iff_specMap (φ : A →ₐ[L] L ⊗[K] B) :
539	    IsEquivariantAlgHom K L A B φ ↔
540	      ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L,
541	        (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) (L ⊗[K] B) γ).hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom)
542	          = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom) ≫ (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A γ).hom := by
543	  have key : ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L,
544	      ((toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) (L ⊗[K] B) γ).hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom)
545	          = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom) ≫ (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A γ).hom)
546	        ↔ ∀ x : A, γ⁻¹ • φ x = φ (γ⁻¹ • x) := by
547	    intro γ
548	    rw [toSpecAut_hom, toSpecAut_hom, ← Spec.map_comp, ← Spec.map_comp,
549	      ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
550	    constructor
551	    · intro h
552	      have h2 := congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (Spec.map_injective h)
553	      rw [CommRingCat.hom_ofHom, CommRingCat.hom_ofHom] at h2
554	      exact fun x => DFunLike.congr_fun h2 x
555	    · intro h
556	      congr 1
557	      exact CommRingCat.hom_ext (RingHom.ext h)
558	  constructor
559	  · intro hφ γ
560	    rw [key γ]
561	    intro x
562	    rw [galTensor_smul_def, ← hφ γ⁻¹ x]
563	  · intro hs γ x
564	    have h3 := (key γ⁻¹).mp (hs γ⁻¹) x
565	    rw [inv_inv, galTensor_smul_def] at h3
566	    exact h3.symm
567	
568	open Algebra in
569	/-- **The affine case of the Galois quotient Hom property** (campaign `G2(b)`,
570	scheme form, affine `T`).  For `X' = Spec A` with a semilinear `Γ`-action and any
571	affine `T = Spec B` over `Spec K` (with `T ×_{Spec K} Spec L = Spec (L ⊗[K] B)`):
572	morphisms `T ⟶ Spec (A^Γ)` over `Spec K` correspond to `Γ`-equivariant morphisms
573	`Spec (L ⊗[K] B) ⟶ Spec A` over `Spec L`.  Proved by Speiser descent
574	(`invariantAlgHomEquiv`), never via invariant finiteness. -/
575	noncomputable def affineGaloisQuotientHomEquiv :
576	    {t : Spec (CommRingCat.of B) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of (invariantsSubalgebra K L A)) //
577	      t ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (invariantsSubalgebra K L A)))
578	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K B))} ≃
579	    {h : Spec (CommRingCat.of (L ⊗[K] B)) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A) //
580	      (h ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L A))
581	          = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L (L ⊗[K] B)))) ∧
582	      ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L,
583	        (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) (L ⊗[K] B) γ).hom ≫ h
584	          = h ≫ (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A γ).hom} :=
585	  ((specOverEquivAlgHom K (invariantsSubalgebra K L A) B).trans
586	    ((invariantAlgHomEquiv K L A B).trans
587	      ((Equiv.subtypeEquiv (specOverEquivAlgHom L A (L ⊗[K] B)).symm
588	        (fun φ => isEquivariantAlgHom_iff_specMap K L A B φ)).trans
589	        (Equiv.subtypeSubtypeEquivSubtypeInter _ _))))
590	
591	end AffineHomProperty
592	
593	end AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

10	/-! # Widened divisor representability for the challenge curve -/

12	set_option autoImplicit false

29	section Curve
30	
31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
32	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
33	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
34	
35	/-- The finite dominant map to `P¹` used by both the divisor representer and the Picard
36	coverage parameter. -/
37	noncomputable def divRepAffP1Map : C.left ⟶ P1 k :=
38	  (exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1 (C := C)).choose
39	
40	noncomputable instance divRepAffP1Map_isFinite : IsFinite (divRepAffP1Map C) :=
41	  (exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1 (C := C)).choose_spec.1
42	
43	noncomputable instance divRepAffP1Map_isDominant : IsDominant (divRepAffP1Map C) :=
44	  (exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1 (C := C)).choose_spec.2.1
45	
46	/-- The chosen map is a morphism over the base field. -/
47	theorem divRepAffP1Map_comp :
48	    divRepAffP1Map C ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom :=
49	  (exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1 (C := C)).choose_spec.2.2
50	
51	/-- The unconditional Picard coverage parameter attached to the same map used by the
52	divisor representer. -/
53	noncomputable def divRepAffAdmissibleParameter : ℕ := by
54	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
55	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
56	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
57	  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
58	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
59	    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
60	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
61	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
62	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
63	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
64	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
65	    moduleFinite_hModule_one C
66	  exact admissibleCoverageParameter (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) (genus C)
67	
68	/-- The curve genus is at most the unconditional admissible coverage parameter. -/
69	theorem genus_le_divRepAffAdmissibleParameter :
70	    genus C ≤ divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C := by
71	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
72	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
73	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
74	  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
75	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
76	    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
77	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
78	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
79	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
80	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
81	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
82	    moduleFinite_hModule_one C
83	  change genus C ≤
84	    admissibleCoverageParameter (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) (genus C)
85	  by_cases hg : genus C = 0
86	  · omega
87	  · exact Nat.le_of_lt
88	      (genus_lt_admissibleCoverageParameter_of_ne_zero
89	        (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) (genus C) hg (chi_moduleKSheaf C))
90	
91	/-- A representer for the widened divisor functor at the genus of a challenge curve.  The finite
92	dominant map to `P1`, the cohomology finiteness instances, and the Euler-characteristic identities
93	are all chosen internally from the curve assumptions. -/
94	noncomputable def divFunctorAffGenusRepresenter :
95	    Σ D : Over (Spec (.of k)), (divFunctorAff C (genus C)).RepresentableBy D := by
96	  classical
97	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
98	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
99	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
100	  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
101	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
102	    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
103	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
104	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
105	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
106	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
107	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
108	    moduleFinite_hModule_one C
109	  have hpi : divRepAffP1Map C ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (.of k) :=
110	    divRepAffP1Map_comp C
111	  let D := divRepAffScheme_at (C := C) (pi := divRepAffP1Map C)
112	    (hpi := hpi) (g := genus C) (hO := h0_moduleKSheaf C)
113	    (gamma := genus C) (hgamma := Nat.le_refl _) (hchiGamma := chi_moduleKSheaf C)
114	  exact ⟨D, divFunctorAff_representableBy_at
115	    (C := C) (pi := divRepAffP1Map C) (hpi := hpi)
116	    (g := genus C) (hO := h0_moduleKSheaf C)
117	    (gamma := genus C) (hgamma := Nat.le_refl _) (hchiGamma := chi_moduleKSheaf C)⟩
118	
119	/-- A chosen scheme representing the widened divisor functor at the curve's genus. -/
120	noncomputable def divRepAffGenusScheme : Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
121	  (divFunctorAffGenusRepresenter C).1
122	
123	/-- The widened divisor functor at the genus of a challenge curve is representable, with no
124	additional hypotheses. -/
125	noncomputable def divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy :
126	    (divFunctorAff C (genus C)).RepresentableBy (divRepAffGenusScheme C) :=
127	  (divFunctorAffGenusRepresenter C).2
128	
129	/-- A representer for the widened divisor functor at the unconditional Picard coverage
130	parameter. The curve genus controls Euler-characteristic normalization independently of the
131	larger divisor degree. -/
132	noncomputable def divFunctorAffAdmissibleRepresenter :
133	    Σ D : Over (Spec (.of k)),
134	      (divFunctorAff C (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C)).RepresentableBy D := by
135	  classical
136	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
137	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
138	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
139	  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
140	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
141	    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
142	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
143	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
144	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
145	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
146	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
147	    moduleFinite_hModule_one C
148	  have hpi : divRepAffP1Map C ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (.of k) :=
149	    divRepAffP1Map_comp C
150	  let D := divRepAffScheme_at (C := C) (pi := divRepAffP1Map C)
151	    (hpi := hpi) (g := divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (hO := h0_moduleKSheaf C)

8	/-!
9	# Functoriality of the WIDENED vehicle along an arbitrary test morphism (R2, residue (b))
10	
11	The widened vehicle `divFamZarAff` (`…AffVehicle.lean`) is functorial along an **arbitrary**
12	morphism `f : T' ⟶ T` of test objects: the value of the restricted family at an affine open
13	`W ⊆ T'.left` — whose `f`-image need not lie in any affine open of `T.left` — is *glued* over a
14	finite basic-open refinement of `W` subordinate to the preimages of affine opens, using the
15	widened S5b Zariski keystones through the basic-open toolkit (`…AffMapKit.lean`).
16	
17	This is the last packaging layer of R2 residue (b): with it the widened carrier of protection
18	I-0492 is a functor on the whole slice over `Spec k`, which is the generality every DD-R
19	consumer (`DivRepGlobalData.pull_comp`) is stated at.
20	
21	## Main declarations
22	
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAff.IsPullbackValue` — the characterizing property of the glued
24	  value, with `pullbackValue_unique` (Zariski separation) and `exists_isPullbackValue`
25	  (Zariski gluing).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAff.map C n f : divFamZarAff C n T → divFamZarAff C n T'`, with
27	  `map_id`, `map_comp`, and the no-gluing evaluation `mapVal_eq_mapAlgHom`.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_naturality` — over affine tests, `map` along
29	  `Spec` of an algebra map is `DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom` of that map under the widened affine
30	  collapse.
31	
32	## What is and is not asserted
33	
34	Everything here is about the Zariski topology of the **base**.  R2 widened the curve side, so
35	these are the chart-typed proofs of `DivisorFamilyZarMap.lean` with `DivFamZar` replaced by
36	`DivFamZarAff` — no new geometry, and in particular **no `|P¹(k)|` hypothesis** anywhere in the
37	statements or their route.  What the widened lane still owes is unchanged by this file: the
38	subordinate Stacks 0B8B input (residue (a), out of scope per I-0492 clause 2).
39	-/
40

43	values over them, which are stated on the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left`; see

64	/-! ## The characterizing property of the glued value -/
65	
66	variable (C n) in
67	/-- The characterizing property of the value at `W` of the restriction of `s` along `f`: on
68	every affine sub-open of `W` contained in the preimage of an affine open `V` of the target, it
69	restricts to the base change of the value of `s` at `V`. -/
70	def IsPullbackValue (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZarAff C n T) (W : T'.left.affineOpens)
71	    (v : DivFamZarAff C Γ(T'.left, W.1) n) : Prop :=
72	  ∀ (W₀ : T'.left.affineOpens) (hW₀ : W₀.1 ≤ W.1) (V : T.left.affineOpens)
73	    (hV : W₀.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
74	    DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T' hW₀) v
75	      = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W₀.1 hV) (s.1 V)
76	
77	/-- Values with the pullback property are unique — from the Zariski separation of
78	`DivFamZarAff` over a basic refinement subordinate to the preimages of affine opens. -/
79	theorem pullbackValue_unique {f : T' ⟶ T} {s : divFamZarAff C n T}
80	    {W : T'.left.affineOpens} {v v' : DivFamZarAff C Γ(T'.left, W.1) n}
81	    (hv : IsPullbackValue C n f s W v) (hv' : IsPullbackValue C n f s W v') :
82	    v = v' := by
83	  classical
84	  obtain ⟨sub, hspan, hsub⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover W.2
85	    (fun U₀ => ∃ V : T.left.affineOpens, U₀ = f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1)
86	    (fun w _ => by
87	      obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hfwV, -⟩ := Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp
88	        T.left.isBasis_affineOpens (show f.left.base w ∈ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) from trivial)
89	      exact ⟨f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V, hfwV, ⟨⟨V, hVaff⟩, rfl⟩⟩)
90	  refine eq_of_basic_eq W sub hspan (fun r hr => ?_)
91	  obtain ⟨U₀, ⟨V, rfl⟩, hle⟩ := hsub r hr
92	  rw [hv ⟨_, W.2.basicOpen r⟩ (T'.left.basicOpen_le r) V hle,
93	    hv' ⟨_, W.2.basicOpen r⟩ (T'.left.basicOpen_le r) V hle]
94	
95	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
96	-- The instance towers over the section rings of the basic refinement exceed the default
97	-- elaboration budget (as in the chart-typed `divFamZar.exists_isPullbackValue`).
98	/-- **Existence of the glued value**: the restriction of a compatible family of widened classes
99	along an arbitrary morphism of test objects has a value at every affine open of the source,
100	glued over a finite basic-open refinement subordinate to the preimages of affine opens — the
101	widened S5b gluing keystone through `divFamZarAff.exists_glue_of_basic_compat`. -/
102	theorem exists_isPullbackValue (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZarAff C n T)
103	    (W : T'.left.affineOpens) : ∃ v, IsPullbackValue C n f s W v := by
104	  classical
105	  -- the basic refinement subordinate to preimages of affine opens
106	  obtain ⟨sub, hspan, hsub⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover W.2
107	    (fun U₀ => ∃ V : T.left.affineOpens, U₀ = f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1)
108	    (fun w _ => by
109	      obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hfwV, -⟩ := Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp
110	        T.left.isBasis_affineOpens (show f.left.base w ∈ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) from trivial)
111	      exact ⟨f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V, hfwV, ⟨⟨V, hVaff⟩, rfl⟩⟩)
112	  have hsub' : ∀ r ∈ sub, ∃ V : T.left.affineOpens,
113	      T'.left.basicOpen r ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 := fun r hr => by
114	    obtain ⟨U₀, ⟨V, rfl⟩, hle⟩ := hsub r hr
115	    exact ⟨V, hle⟩
116	  choose Vc hVc using hsub'
117	  have hbmul : ∀ r r' : ↥sub,
118	      T'.left.basicOpen ((r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) * (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))
119	        ≤ T'.left.basicOpen (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) := fun r r' => by
120	    rw [Scheme.basicOpen_mul]
121	    exact inf_le_left
122	  have hbmul' : ∀ r r' : ↥sub,
123	      T'.left.basicOpen ((r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) * (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))
124	        ≤ T'.left.basicOpen (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) := fun r r' => by
125	    rw [Scheme.basicOpen_mul]
126	    exact inf_le_right
127	  -- glue the local base changes over the basic refinement
128	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := exists_glue_of_basic_compat W sub hspan
129	    (fun r : ↥sub => DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
130	      (Over.appLEAlgHom f (Vc r.1 r.2).1 (T'.left.basicOpen r.1) (hVc r.1 r.2))
131	      (s.1 (Vc r.1 r.2)))
132	    hbmul hbmul'
133	    (fun r r' => by
134	      -- the overlap compatibility, from choice independence
135	      rw [← DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp, ← DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp,
136	        Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom, Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom]
137	      exact mapAlgHom_appLE_eq C n f s (W₀ := ⟨_, W.2.basicOpen (r.1 * r'.1)⟩) _ _)
138	  -- the glued value has the pullback property
139	  refine ⟨z, fun W₀ hW₀ V hV => ?_⟩
140	  obtain ⟨sub₀, hspan₀, hsub₀⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover W₀.2
141	    (fun U₀ => ∃ r ∈ sub, U₀ = T'.left.basicOpen r)
142	    (fun w hw => by
143	      have hwW : w ∈ (⨆ r ∈ (↑sub : Set Γ(T'.left, W.1)), T'.left.basicOpen r) := by
144	        rw [iSup_basicOpen_of_span_eq_top _ _ hspan]
145	        exact hW₀ hw
146	      obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp hwW
147	      obtain ⟨hrsub, hwr⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp hr
148	      exact ⟨T'.left.basicOpen r, hwr, ⟨r, hrsub, rfl⟩⟩)
149	  refine eq_of_basic_eq W₀ sub₀ hspan₀ (fun q hq => ?_)
150	  obtain ⟨U₀, ⟨r, hr, rfl⟩, hqle⟩ := hsub₀ q hq
151	  -- the left side restricts through the glued datum
152	  have hzr : DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
153	        (Over.resAlgHom T' (T'.left.basicOpen_le r)) z
154	      = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
155	          (Over.appLEAlgHom f (Vc r hr).1 (T'.left.basicOpen r) (hVc r hr))
156	          (s.1 (Vc r hr)) := hz ⟨r, hr⟩
157	  have hL : DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T' (T'.left.basicOpen_le q))
158	      (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T' hW₀) z)
159	      = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f (Vc r hr).1 (T'.left.basicOpen q)
160	          (hqle.trans (hVc r hr))) (s.1 (Vc r hr)) := by
161	    rw [← DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp,
162	      show ((T'.left.basicOpen_le q).trans hW₀ :
163	          T'.left.basicOpen q ≤ W.1)
164	        = (hqle.trans (T'.left.basicOpen_le r)) from rfl,
165	      ← Over.resAlgHom_comp T' hqle (T'.left.basicOpen_le r),
166	      DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp, hzr, ← DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp,
167	      Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom]
168	  -- the right side restricts directly
169	  rw [hL, ← DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom]
170	  exact mapAlgHom_appLE_eq C n f s (W₀ := ⟨_, W₀.2.basicOpen q⟩) _ _
171	
172	/-- Existence and uniqueness of the glued value. -/
173	theorem existsUnique_isPullbackValue (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZarAff C n T)
174	    (W : T'.left.affineOpens) : ∃! v, IsPullbackValue C n f s W v := by
175	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := exists_isPullbackValue f s W
176	  exact ⟨v, hv, fun v' hv' => pullbackValue_unique hv' hv⟩
177	
178	/-! ## The functoriality -/
179	
180	variable (C n)
181	
182	/-- The value of the restricted widened family at an affine open of the source. -/
183	noncomputable def mapVal (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZarAff C n T)
184	    (W : T'.left.affineOpens) : DivFamZarAff C Γ(T'.left, W.1) n :=
185	  (existsUnique_isPullbackValue f s W).choose
186	
187	lemma mapVal_spec (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZarAff C n T) (W : T'.left.affineOpens) :
188	    IsPullbackValue C n f s W (mapVal C n f s W) :=
189	  (existsUnique_isPullbackValue f s W).choose_spec.1
190	
191	lemma mapVal_eq_of (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZarAff C n T) {W : T'.left.affineOpens}
192	    {v : DivFamZarAff C Γ(T'.left, W.1) n} (hv : IsPullbackValue C n f s W v) :
193	    mapVal C n f s W = v :=
194	  pullbackValue_unique (mapVal_spec C n f s W) hv
195	
196	/-- The value of the restricted widened family on an affine open lying in the preimage of an
197	affine open is the plain base change — no gluing. -/
198	lemma mapVal_eq_mapAlgHom (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZarAff C n T)
199	    {W : T'.left.affineOpens} {V : T.left.affineOpens} (hV : W.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) :
200	    mapVal C n f s W
201	      = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W.1 hV) (s.1 V) := by
202	  have h := mapVal_spec C n f s W W le_rfl V hV
203	  rwa [Over.resAlgHom_rfl, DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_id] at h
204	
205	/-- **Restriction of the widened vehicle along an arbitrary morphism of test objects** — the
206	last packaging layer of R2 residue (b): the value at each affine open of the source is the
207	glued pullback value. -/
208	noncomputable def map (f : T' ⟶ T) : divFamZarAff C n T → divFamZarAff C n T' :=
209	  fun s =>
210	    ⟨fun W => mapVal C n f s W, by
211	      intro U V h
212	      beta_reduce
213	      refine (mapVal_eq_of C n f s (W := U) ?_).symm
214	      intro W₀ hW₀ V' hV'
215	      rw [← DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp]
216	      exact mapVal_spec C n f s V W₀ (hW₀.trans h) V' hV'⟩
217	
218	@[simp]
219	lemma map_val (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZarAff C n T) (W : T'.left.affineOpens) :
220	    (map C n f s).1 W = mapVal C n f s W :=
221	  rfl
222	
223	/-- The functor law: restriction along the identity is the identity. -/
224	theorem map_id (s : divFamZarAff C n T) : map C n (𝟙 T) s = s := by
225	  refine ext fun W => ?_
226	  rw [map_val]
227	  refine mapVal_eq_of C n (𝟙 T) s ?_
228	  intro W₀ hW₀ V hV
229	  have hV' : W₀.1 ≤ V.1 := by
230	    intro p hp
231	    have hmem := hV hp
232	    rw [Over.id_left] at hmem
233	    exact hmem
234	  rw [Over.appLEAlgHom_id T V.1 W₀.1 hV hV', s.compat W₀ W hW₀, s.compat W₀ V hV']
235	
236	/-- The functor law: restriction along a composite is the composite of the restrictions. -/
237	theorem map_comp (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T'' ⟶ T') (s : divFamZarAff C n T) :
238	    map C n (g ≫ f) s = map C n g (map C n f s) := by
239	  classical
240	  refine ext fun W => ?_
241	  rw [map_val, map_val]
242	  refine (mapVal_eq_of C n (g ≫ f) s ?_)
243	  intro W₀ hW₀ V hV
244	  -- refine by basic opens whose `g`-image lies in an affine open inside `f⁻¹ V`
245	  obtain ⟨sub, hspan, hsub⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover W₀.2
246	    (fun U₀ => ∃ V'' : T'.left.affineOpens,
247	      V''.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 ∧ U₀ = g.left ⁻¹ᵁ V''.1)
248	    (fun w hw => by
249	      have hgw : g.left.base w ∈ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 := by
250	        have := hV hw
251	        rw [Over.comp_left] at this
252	        exact this
253	      obtain ⟨V'', hV''aff, hgwV'', hV''le⟩ := Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp
254	        T'.left.isBasis_affineOpens hgw
255	      exact ⟨g.left ⁻¹ᵁ V'', hgwV'', ⟨⟨V'', hV''aff⟩, hV''le, rfl⟩⟩)
256	  refine eq_of_basic_eq W₀ sub hspan (fun q hq => ?_)
257	  obtain ⟨U₀, ⟨V'', hV''le, rfl⟩, hqle⟩ := hsub q hq
258	  -- the left side, through the two glued values
259	  have hL : DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T'' (T''.left.basicOpen_le q))
260	      (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T'' hW₀)
261	        (mapVal C n g (map C n f s) W))
262	      = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom g V''.1 (T''.left.basicOpen q) hqle)
263	          (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 V''.1 hV''le) (s.1 V)) := by
264	    rw [← DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp,
265	      mapVal_spec C n g (map C n f s) W ⟨_, W₀.2.basicOpen q⟩
266	        ((T''.left.basicOpen_le q).trans hW₀) V'' hqle,
267	      map_val, mapVal_eq_mapAlgHom C n f s hV''le]
268	  rw [hL, ← DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp, ← DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp,
269	    Over.appLEAlgHom_comp f g V.1 V''.1 (T''.left.basicOpen q) hV''le hqle
270	      (hqle.trans ((g.left.preimage_mono hV''le).trans
271	        (le_of_eq (by rw [Over.comp_left, Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage])))),
272	    Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom]
273	
274	end divFamZarAff

276	/-! ## The widened divisor functor -/
277	
278	section Functor
279	
280	/- `C` and `n` are file-level IMPLICIT variables; the `variable (C n)` that made them explicit
281	lived inside `namespace divFamZarAff` and ended with it.  Without re-declaring them here,
282	`divFunctorAff` takes them implicitly and the `simp` lemmas below — which apply it to `C` and
283	`n` — do not elaborate. -/
284	variable (C n)
285	
286	/-- **The widened divisor functor**: the R2 carrier of protection I-0492 as a presheaf of types
287	on the slice over `Spec k`, with the glued restriction `divFamZarAff.map` along arbitrary test
288	morphisms.  The widened mirror of `divFunctor` (`DivisorFamilyZarFunctor.lean`), and the
289	generality `DivRepGlobalData.pull_comp` consumes. -/
290	noncomputable def divFunctorAff : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u where
291	  obj T := divFamZarAff C n T.unop
292	  map g := ↾divFamZarAff.map C n g.unop
293	  map_id T := by
294	    ext s U
295	    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZarAff C n T.unop => z.1 U) (divFamZarAff.map_id C n s)
296	  map_comp {T T' T''} g h := by
297	    ext s U
298	    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZarAff C n T''.unop => z.1 U)
299	      (divFamZarAff.map_comp C n g.unop h.unop s)
300	
301	@[simp]
302	lemma divFunctorAff_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
303	    (divFunctorAff C n).obj T = divFamZarAff C n T.unop :=
304	  rfl
305	
306	@[simp]
307	lemma divFunctorAff_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
308	    (s : divFamZarAff C n T.unop) :
309	    (divFunctorAff C n).map g s = divFamZarAff.map C n g.unop s :=
310	  rfl
311	
312	end Functor

314	/-! ## Naturality of the widened affine comparison -/
315	
316	section AffineNaturality
317	
318	variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
319	
320	/-- The widened affine comparison intertwines the section-ring pullback along `Spec` of an
321	algebra map with the algebra map itself (local copy of the `PicEtMap` helper). -/
322	private lemma overSpecΓTop_appLE_comp_aff (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) :
323	    (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k B).toAlgHom.comp
324	      (Over.appLEAlgHom (Over.overSpecMap φ) (overSpecTopAffine A).1
325	        (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top)
326	      = φ.comp (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom := by
327	  have key : (Over.overSpecMap φ).left.appLE (overSpecTopAffine A).1
328	        (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B)).hom
329	      = (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).hom ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom := by
330	    have h₁ : (Over.overSpecMap φ).left.appLE (overSpecTopAffine A).1
331	          (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top
332	        = (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom)).appTop :=
333	      Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app _
334	    rw [h₁]
335	    exact Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom)
336	  ext x
337	  exact congr($(key).hom x)
338	
339	/-- **Naturality of the widened affine comparison**: over affine tests, `divFamZarAff.map` along
340	`Spec` of an algebra map corresponds to `DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom` of that map under the widened
341	collapse `divFamZarAffAffineEquiv`.
342	
343	This is the coherence that carries the widened certificate lane's endpoint (which lands at an
344	affine test) into the functor: the glued general-test restriction agrees with the widened total
345	base change wherever both are defined. -/
346	theorem divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_naturality (φ : A →ₐ[k] B)
347	    (s : divFamZarAff C n (overSpec k A)) :
348	    divFamZarAffAffineEquiv C n B (divFamZarAff.map C n (Over.overSpecMap φ) s)
349	      = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φ (divFamZarAffAffineEquiv C n A s) := by
350	  rw [divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_apply, divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_apply, divFamZarAff.map_val]
351	  have hval := divFamZarAff.mapVal_eq_mapAlgHom C n (Over.overSpecMap φ) s
352	    (W := overSpecTopAffine B) (V := overSpecTopAffine A) le_top
353	  rw [hval]
354	  calc DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k B).toAlgHom
355	        (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom (Over.overSpecMap φ)
356	          (overSpecTopAffine A).1 (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top)
357	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)))
358	      = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom ((Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k B).toAlgHom.comp
359	          (Over.appLEAlgHom (Over.overSpecMap φ)
360	            (overSpecTopAffine A).1 (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top))
361	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) := (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp _ _ _).symm
362	    _ = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (φ.comp (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom)
363	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) := by
364	        rw [overSpecΓTop_appLE_comp_aff φ]
365	    _ = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φ (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
366	          (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A))) :=
367	        DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp _ _ _
368	
369	end AffineNaturality
370	
371	end AlgebraicGeometry
